Today's international headlines:
- German Chancellor Merz calls state election a 'disaster' for his party but vows to stay on: Exit polls show damaging losses for Merz's centre-right CDU party in the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin.
- Trump says triumphal arch will be military complex with drones and snipers: Trump said the updated plans were at the request of the US military and for national security purposes.
- Man, 82, dies after beach fight with 76-year-old over sunlounger in Greece: One eyewitness said the scene was so chaotic that screaming could be heard from the other end of the beach.
- Sister of Pakistan's ex-PM Imran Khan arrested: Aleema Khanum is accused of mobilising her brother’s supporters ahead of country-wide protests.
- 'I don't even know if my parents are alive' - the war heroes jailed 25 years ago: The children of key politicians jailed 25 years ago without a trace in Eritrea want answers.
- Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks: An embattled Trump has injected his fight with the news media with new acrimony, writes the BBC's Anthony Zurcher.
- Tata Sons: India's corporate crown braces for upheaval amid boardroom revolt: The Tata boardroom battle has intensified over a re-appointment of its chairman and a diktat to go public.
- Watch: Dramatic moment a cargo ship crashes into another vessel: Verified footage appears to show a cargo ship colliding with a fishing boat near Singapore, with investigators still working to establish exactly when and how the crash happened.
- Watch: BBC tracks down abusive teacher secretly released early: BBC Eye has discovered a teacher who was imprisoned for sexually assaulting a student in Indonesia has been secretly released early.
- Watch: Fans react as Ed Sheeran speaks out over Macklemore controversy at show: Ed Sheeran told the crowd he had made mistakes after Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian remarks.
- 'Enough is enough': Women protest after string of murders near Johannesburg: The police have since set up a task team to investigate the murders and have urged women in the Kempton Park area to avoid walking or running alone "particularly in isolated areas".
- Is the Kennedy Center losing 'hundreds of millions of dollars'?: Records in 2024 show the venue had a surplus of millions of dollars once contributions and grants had been factored in.
